title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rotary/rope optimizations
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Our inference runtime sees a disproportionate amount of CPU/GPU cycles spent in attention kernels for long-context Transformer workloads (chat, long-document). This PR upgrades our FlashAttention integration to the FlashAttentionV2 kernels, introduces fused QKV+proj kernels for common block sizes, and fixes rotary/RoPE handling so fused kernels produce numerically-identical results to the previous implementation. Motivation: reduce p99 token latency, improve throughput for long-sequence workloads, and reduce memory bandwidth pressure in KV cache operations. Summary of changes: - Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernel dispatch and runtime feature flag (gpu/flashattn_v2_enabled). - Add fused qkv+proj CUDA kernels for common head sizes (32, 64) with both fp16 and int8 support paths. - Rework RoPE/rotary position application to be applied inside fused kernels (avoids extra GEMM passes and memory writes). - Refactor KV cache layout to align with fused kernel expectations (packed key-value blocks to reduce memcopy). - Add scheduling hints to the continuous batching scheduler to prefer batch-colocation of requests with similar seq-len/num-heads to increase fusion opportunities. - Add unit and integration tests comparing outputs against baseline (numerical tolerance), and end-to-end perf harness runs in perf-canary. Rollout plan: gated behind runtime flag gpu/flashattn_v2_enabled (off by default). Will enable in canary infra and run 48h throughput/latency comparison and production canary rollout with auto-rollback on regressions. Backwards compatibility: behavior unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled; KV cache on-disk format unchanged, in-memory layout changed only when flag is active. Checklist: - [x] Kernel integration and dispatch - [x] Numeric parity tests - [x] Performance microbenchmarks - [x] End-to-end latency/throughput canary runs - [x] Documentation and release notes - [x] Observability: added metrics for fused-kernel utilization and fusion hit-rate

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a couple of nit comments on kernel naming and a question about fp32 fallback paths. Please add a microbenchmark script for head=16 as well.
Asha Patel: Answered: fp32 falls back to the reference kernel; added microbench for head=16 in perf-canary workloads.
Clara Nguyen: Requested explicit numeric parity tests for 1) fp16, 2) int8-quantized, and 3) small batch sizes — please include in CI.
Asha Patel: Added parity tests and a small-batch job that runs as part of the integration matrix. All tests pass locally and on CI.
Ravi Shah: Approved after validating perf numbers on an A100 canary node (1.35x throughput on seq=4096, 0.9x token-p99 latency improvement for bursty traffic).
performance_summary: Microbenchmarks show 1.25-1.6x throughput improvement for long sequences (seq >= 2048) depending on head size; observed 8-18% p99 token-latency reductions on representative chat workloads in perf-canary. Fusion hit-rate in the canary was ~62% after scheduler changes.
regressions_and_fixes: Initial integration caused a small numeric drift (~1e-4) for fp16 in the first implementation of RoPE in-fusion; fixed by correcting the complex rotation ordering and adding stable accumulation. Also resolved an intermittent OOM by aligning KV packing to 256-byte GPU page boundaries.
rollback_plan: Feature controlled by gpu/flashattn_v2_enabled. Canary rollout for 48h; automatic rollback if throughput drops >5% or p99 increases >10% compared to baseline. Ops runbook updated to revert the flag and restart pools.
release_notes: Upgrade: FlashAttentionV2 + fused QKV+proj kernels with RoPE applied in-kernel. Expect up to ~1.6x throughput for long-context models and improved p99 latency. Feature behind runtime flag gpu/flashattn_v2_enabled.
